newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close lower after inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close lower after inflation data.

text.p: Chilean shares closed slightly lower on Tuesday as profit-taking and news of higher-than-expected inflation in January undercut the market's forward momentum, dealers said.
Still, traders were confident the bolsa would recover its positive tone at the opening.
"The market should maintain its upward trend tomorrow as the impact of the inflation news will be short," one dealer said.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended down 0.04 percent at 111.75 points. The general .IGPA index shed 0.33 percent to 5,231.5 points in light volume of 9.1 billion pesos.
Traders said the stock market reacted negatively to government figures showing that consumer prices rose 0.5 percent in January, exceeding analysts' forecasts of a 0.4 percent increase.
Investors are concerned that signs that inflation was not firmly under control could lead the central bank to delay cutting interest rates.
Investors were also waiting for any word of a possible change in U.S. interest rates as a two-day Federal Reserve policy meeting got under way on Tuesday, dealers said.
Telecom Telex climbed on foreign buy orders after news that the company and rival carrier CTC settled long-running legal disputes.
Telex gained two percent to 1,020 pesos.
Publisher Cochrane continued to rally on news that the company won a large deal in Brazil. Cochrane rose 2.52 percent to 122 pesos.

Declining issues included steelmaker Cap, down 3.23 percent at 1,200 pesos, glass producer Cristales, down 2.93 percent at 2,815 pesos, and copper products manufacturer Madeco, which shed 1.3 percent at 1,140 pesos.
